sections.section: Personal Crisis: Loneliness and Cultural Lies
sections.summary: David Brooks shares his personal crisis in 2013 — his marriage ended, his children left home, and he lost friends. Living alone, consumed by work, he experienced profound loneliness and realized the emptiness in his life reflected the lies our culture tells us.
sections.summaryKo: 데이비드 브룩스가 2013년의 개인적 위기를 나눠요. 결혼 생활이 끝나고, 아이들이 떠나고, 친구들을 잃었어요. 혼자 살면서 일에만 매달렸고, 깊은 외로움을 경험하며 삶의 공허함이 문화가 말하는 거짓말을 반영한다는 것을 깨달았어요.
keyPoints: Personal crisis: divorce, children leaving, loss of friends
Loneliness manifested as fear and lack of solidity
The emptiness outside reflected emptiness within

sections.summary: Brooks identifies three cultural lies: (1) career success is fulfilling, (2) you can make yourself happy through self-sufficiency, and (3) the meritocracy — the belief that your worth equals your accomplishments. He argues that deep relationships, not achievements, create true happiness.
sections.summaryKo: 브룩스는 세 가지 문화적 거짓말을 지적해요. (1) 직업적 성공이 만족을 준다, (2) 자급자족으로 행복해질 수 있다, (3) 능력주의 — 당신의 가치가 성취와 같다는 믿음이에요. 성취가 아니라 깊은 관계가 진정한 행복을 만든다고 주장해요.
keyPoints: Career success only avoids shame, doesn't bring positive good
Self-sufficiency is a lie; deep relationships make people happy
Meritocracy teaches conditional love and dehumanizing rankings

sections.summary: Brooks describes how his personal valley of disconnection mirrors a national crisis. He presents alarming statistics about loneliness, isolation, depression, and suicide in America, arguing that we face not just economic and environmental crises but a social and relational one.
sections.summaryKo: 브룩스는 자신의 단절의 골짜기가 국가적 위기를 반영한다고 설명해요. 미국의 외로움, 고립, 우울증, 자살에 관한 충격적인 통계를 제시하며, 경제적 환경적 위기뿐 아니라 사회적이고 관계적인 위기에 직면해 있다고 주장해요.
keyPoints: 35% of Americans over 45 are chronically lonely
Suicide rate has risen 30% since 1999
Life expectancy is falling — a social and relational crisis exists

sections.summary: Brooks shares three realizations from his valley: (1) social freedom without roots leads to drift, (2) suffering can break you or break you open to deeper self-knowledge, and (3) the heart yearns for love and fusion with others. He illustrates with the theologian Paul Tillich and a passage from Captain Corelli's Mandolin.
sections.summaryKo: 브룩스는 골짜기에서 얻은 세 가지 깨달음을 나눠요. (1) 뿌리 없는 사회적 자유는 방황으로 이끈다, (2) 고통은 부서지게도, 열리게도 할 수 있다, (3) 마음은 사랑과 타인과의 융합을 갈망한다는 거예요. 신학자 폴 틸리히와 코렐리 대위의 만돌린을 인용해요.
keyPoints: Freedom is a river to cross, not an ocean to swim in
Suffering carves deeper into the soul, revealing unknown depths
True love is what remains after being in love burns away

sections.summary: Brooks explores the soul and consciousness. He argues that everyone has a soul of infinite dignity regardless of status. The soul yearns for righteousness while the heart yearns for connection. Borrowing from Einstein, he says problems can't be solved at the level of consciousness that created them.
sections.summaryKo: 브룩스는 영혼과 의식을 탐구해요. 지위에 관계없이 모든 사람에게 무한한 존엄성의 영혼이 있다고 주장해요. 영혼은 올바름을 갈망하고 마음은 연결을 갈망해요. 아인슈타인을 인용하여 문제를 만든 의식 수준에서는 문제를 해결할 수 없다고 말해요.
keyPoints: Every person has a soul with infinite dignity and value
The soul yearns for righteousness, the heart for fusion
You must expand to a different level of consciousness to solve problems

sections.summary: Brooks shares stories of 'weavers' — community builders who pull others out of valleys. He describes Kathy and David's home that welcomed 25 kids, Aisha Butler who chose to stay and rebuild her neighborhood, Sarah who turned tragedy into service, and the Roots of Empathy program that teaches children through caring for an infant.
sections.summaryKo: 브룩스는 '위버' — 다른 사람을 골짜기에서 끌어올리는 공동체 건설자들의 이야기를 나눠요. 25명의 아이를 환영한 캐시와 데이비드의 집, 동네를 재건하기로 한 아이샤 버틀러, 비극을 봉사로 바꾼 세라, 아기 돌봄을 통해 아이들에게 공감을 가르치는 공감의 뿌리 프로그램을 소개해요.
keyPoints: You can't climb out of a valley alone — someone must reach in
Weavers live relationist lives with moral motivation and vocational certitude
Stories of Kathy & David, Aisha Butler, Sarah, and Roots of Empathy

sections.section: Happiness vs. Joy: Dissolving the Self
sections.summary: Brooks distinguishes between happiness (expansion of self) and joy (dissolving of self). He uses E.O. Wilson's childhood awe at nature and Zadie Smith's ecstatic night at a London club to illustrate joy — moments when self-consciousness disappears and one is fully given over to the experience.
sections.summaryKo: 브룩스는 행복(자아의 확장)과 기쁨(자아의 용해)을 구분해요. E.O. 윌슨의 자연에 대한 어린 시절의 경외와 재디 스미스의 런던 클럽에서의 황홀한 밤을 통해 기쁨을 설명해요 — 자의식이 사라지고 경험에 완전히 빠지는 순간이에요.
keyPoints: Happiness is expansion of self; joy is dissolving of self
E.O. Wilson's childhood encounter with nature illustrates awe and vocation
Zadie Smith's nightclub experience captures the surrender to joy

sections.section: Two Mindsets: Individual Success vs. Relational Living
sections.summary: Brooks contrasts two mindsets: the 'first mountain' mindset of individual success and the relational mindset needed to heal our national valley. He calls for a cultural and relational revolution, arguing that weavers have found a better way to live, and if we follow their example, both personal emptiness and social fragmentation can be repaired.
sections.summaryKo: 브룩스는 두 가지 사고방식을 대비해요: 개인적 성공의 '첫 번째 산' 사고방식과 국가적 골짜기를 치유하는 데 필요한 관계적 사고방식이에요. 문화적이고 관계적인 혁명을 촉구하며, 위버들이 더 나은 삶의 방식을 찾았고 그 본보기를 따르면 개인의 공허함과 사회적 분열 모두 회복될 수 있다고 주장해요.
keyPoints: Two mindsets: first mountain (individual success) vs. relational living
We need a cultural and relational revolution, not just economic fixes
Weavers show a better way — we just need to shift our lives a little
